A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cache-of-Thought study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original static and dynamic evaluations on MMMU and VL-ICL subtasks, including model comparisons and cache/retrieval analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and cache/retrieval analyses in Sections 5–6, Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–7.

M1.justification: The routing, cached master responses, frozen apprentice models, in-context prompting, dense retrieval and hierarchical retrieval procedures remain unchanged. Identifying hnswlib supplies implementation detail; reinforcement-learning integration and specialized indexes remain future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMMU and the TextOCR and CLEVR subtasks of VL-ICL under the same static and dynamic scenarios. The new UOUO citation does not introduce an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same no-in-context baselines, GPT-4o reference, dense and hierarchical retrieval comparisons, and OpenFlamingo configurations. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 corrects its first column from 'Cache Dev / Test Val' to 'Cache Val / Test Dev'. This revises the reported split assignment to match the two directions already described in v1 Section 6.1, without establishing a rerun. Sample counts, filtering, models, scoring and cache initialization procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The cache-size, retrieval-strategy, cluster-count, initialization, apprentice-usage and temporal cache-growth analyses are retained. The proposed comparison of in-context learning, supervised finetuning and reinforcement learning is future work, not an added analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Section 7.2 adds a qualitative nondeterminism caveat, without introducing statistical estimation or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: After matching the split directions described in Section 6.1, Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–7 retain their results. For example, hierarchical retrieval scores remain 39.04 and 39.44, and Figure 5 retains the 0.077 WarmStart gain at 90% apprentice usage. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The frozen-model assumptions and mathematical formulations of routing, caching, in-context inference and the two-level hashtag structure are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, novelty paragraph and conclusion refocus the stated contribution from VLM inference and general VQA to VLM reasoning and general reasoning. The framework contributions and claimed maximum gains of 7.7% overall and 36.6% for the apprentice remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7.1 expands the applicability discussion to reinforcement-learning-based retrieval from an evolving external memory and future comparisons with supervised finetuning. These are explicitly prospective extensions. Existing explanations of experimental findings and the model/modality limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository URL and code-release statement, identifies hnswlib's built-in filtered search in Section 4.3.2, and names Delta/DeltaAI computing resources. These are additional disclosures; the model specifications, four 40GB A100 GPUs and Appendix A prompts are retained. Repository contents were not checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to UOUO, workload-aware caching, Sieve, hnswlib, VTool-R1 and an inference-nondeterminism blog. These support limited additions about motivation, implementation and future directions; the existing related-work discussion is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and recurring VQA terminology, introduces Future Work and Reproducibility subsections and an Acknowledgement section, and renames 'Example Appendix' to 'Appendix'. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: The same seven figures and three tables are retained, with several charts enlarged and spacing adjusted. Table 3 moves from the left to the right column, and Table 1's duplicated split header is corrected. The appendix prompt-box layout is essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects Table 1's misleading split header, improves chart legibility, and adds code-access information and a concrete filtered-search implementation detail. These improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. The empirical evidence, method and appendix prompts remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
